novel_features.name: System health check
novel_features.description: See one combined go/no-go status for a site instead of cross-referencing several separate calls.
novel_features.rationale: Combines four live calls (details, overview, current-power-flow, inventory) into one healthy/degraded/unknown view that no single endpoint returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this over 'site overview' or 'site current-power-flow' when you need one answer to 'is this site OK right now'.

novel_features.name: Underperformance vs baseline
novel_features.description: Flag days where production fell below this site's own historical average for that time of year.
novel_features.rationale: The raw API has no historical-baseline comparison feature; this computes a trailing average from one 364-day energy call and flags recent days against it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when the question is 'is this normal for this site' rather than 'what changed recently' (use 'site changes' for the latter).

novel_features.name: What changed since X
novel_features.description: Get a short digest of the energy delta vs the prior period of equal length, plus a current equipment-count snapshot.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no diff feature of its own and no equipment-history endpoint, so this computes the delta from one energy call spanning both periods and adds a current (non-delta) inventory count for context.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this for a recent-delta digest; pick 'site underperformance' instead for statistical baseline comparisons.

novel_features.name: Rate-limit budget tracker
novel_features.description: See how much of today's 300-request quota this CLI has used, per site.
novel_features.rationale: No SolarEdge endpoint exposes remaining quota; this is a purely local derived view over a call log that 'site health', 'site underperformance', 'site changes', and 'equipment faults' write to.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Check this before running several site commands in a row so a 429 doesn't interrupt you partway through.

novel_features.name: Equipment fault digest
novel_features.description: See only the inverters, batteries, or system elements in a non-nominal state.
novel_features.rationale: Combines inventory optimizer counts, recent battery telemetry, and current power-flow element status into one filtered view; no endpoint pre-filters to non-nominal equipment.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a filtered fault list; use 'equipment inventory' for the full unfiltered equipment list.

narrative.headline: Every SolarEdge Monitoring API endpoint, plus local history that answers questions the API itself can't.
narrative.value_prop: Existing SolarEdge wrappers (Python, Node, Go, Rust) are thin 1:1 API clients that return exactly what one endpoint gives you. This CLI computes things the API never does on its own: 'site underperformance' flags days statistically below the site's own trailing average, 'site changes' diffs the current period against the prior one, 'site health' combines four calls into a single go/no-go view, and 'budget status' tracks how much of the 300-request/day quota this CLI has used, since the API exposes no header or endpoint for it.
narrative.auth_narrative: SolarEdge issues two kinds of API keys: an Account-level key (Account Admin > Company Details > API Access) that can see every site on the account, or a Site-level key (Site Admin > Site Details > API Access) scoped to one site. Either works with `SOLAREDGE_API_KEY`; account-level keys additionally unlock `accounts list` and bulk multi-site commands.

quickstart.comment: verify the binary and config resolve before touching the network
confirm the API key works and see which sites you can access
check current power, today/month/lifetime energy for a known site
cache your site list locally so 'sites' searches and lookups work offline

troubleshoots.fix: you've hit the 300-requests/day or 3-concurrent-call limit for this account+site; run `solaredge-pp-cli budget status` to see this CLI's tracked usage before retrying
check the requested time window against the endpoint's limit (1 week for storage/sensor/inverter data, 1 month for power/powerDetails, 1 year for daily energy) — narrow the range and retry
confirm SOLAREDGE_API_KEY is set to a key generated from Account Admin or Site Admin > API Access, not a portal password

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you own or manage one or more SolarEdge sites and want offline-queryable production/consumption history, equipment health checks, or fleet-wide rollups without re-deriving them by hand from the raw Monitoring API on every check.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for real-time control of the inverter or battery (the SolarEdge Monitoring API is read-only; use the SetApp mobile app or installer tools for configuration changes)

Do not use this CLI for live home-automation event triggers (e.g. turning on a load when production spikes) — it polls on demand, it does not push events; use Home Assistant or solaredge2mqtt for that
Do not use this CLI to bypass the 300-request/day account limit — it tracks the budget, it cannot raise it

recipes.explanation: One combined go/no-go status instead of cross-referencing overview, power flow, and equipment calls by hand.

recipes.title: Is this normal for this time of year
recipes.explanation: Flags days statistically below this site's own trailing average, the question the raw API can never answer in one call.

recipes.title: Pull only the meter breakdown an agent needs
recipes.explanation: energyDetails returns a verbose nested meters array; --select narrows it to just the meter type and values an agent needs.

recipes.title: Check the daily rate-limit budget before a big sync
recipes.explanation: Shows requests used/remaining against the 300/day cap before kicking off a fleet-wide sync that could trigger a 429.
